_comment: Phase 1-B price-only scoring model config (docs/industry_cycle_mvp_design.md section 7.1/7.2/7.3 applied to price-only inputs; section 12 Phase 1 item 4: '과열·추세 훼손 점수 계산'). Every weight/threshold used by committee.industry_cycle.price_scoring and price_state_machine lives here, never hardcoded in code, so tuning the model never requires a code change (only a new model_version). Changing this file's values without bumping model_version will make old industry_factor_weekly/industry_price_state_weekly rows non-reproducible from the current config -- always bump model_version when the numbers below change.

relative_strength._comment: Higher scale_k makes the logistic squash steeper (a smaller weighted relative-return moves the score further from 50). components are decimal fractions (0.05 == +5%).

trend._comment: components are (price / moving_average - 1); longer MAs weigh more because they confirm a more durable trend.

overheat._comment: ma200_gap reused as a long-term extension proxy; return_1m captures short-term acceleration; volume_change captures a turnover surge.

price_risk._comment: drawdown_severity = -(drawdown_from_52w_high), always >= 0. vol_60d's weight is set much higher than drawdown/below_ma_ratio because its natural magnitude (~0.01-0.05) is roughly 10x smaller; this is a deliberate scale-compensation choice of a rule-based v1 model, not a statistically normalized one -- see price_scoring.py module docstring. Unlike the other three score groups (whose raw inputs are already centered at 0), every price_risk raw component is >= 0 by construction, so 'baselines' defines what a NEUTRAL/typical value looks like for each -- subtracted before weighting so the score can also signal below-average risk (score < 50), not just above-average.
